prompt: The design proposes two labelled views: `direct` (a row's own executions) and `inclusive` (direct + revision-child descendants), with board-level totals summing `direct` ONLY. A row's detail view would lead with `inclusive`. Revision children hold ~20% of cache-read and ~21% of output, so ignoring them under-counts a chore by that much, while summing `inclusive` board-wide double-counts that same slice. Confirm the semantics?
choices: Yes — two views, detail leads with `inclusive`, board sums `direct` only (recommended)
Two views, but the detail view should lead with `direct` and show `inclusive` beside it
One view only — `direct` everywhere; accept the ~20% under-count on chores
One view only — `inclusive` everywhere; forbid board-level totals entirely

prompt: `pr_review` executions attach to the same work item (118 runs, 140M cache-read). The design counts them as spend but never blends them into a single number: every figure reports an `implementation` / `design` / `overhead` class split alongside the total. Confirm?
choices: Yes — include, always with the three-way class split shown (recommended)
Include, but as a single blended total with no class split
Exclude `pr_review` and `automation_triage` from a work item's figure entirely
Include, but split only two ways: implementation vs everything-else

prompt: Where should the model rate table live? Since 2026-07-31 an in-code constant table already exists (`engine/core/src/cost_pricing.rs`, `MODEL_PRICING`): three Anthropic families, substring-matched, no source URL, no retrieval date, no effective dating. Rate changes are a human decision with money attached, so the design assumes version-controlled and code-reviewed rather than runtime-editable, and proposes replacing that constant with a dated, provenance-bearing table in its own crate (entry 13).
choices: Version-controlled data file in the repo with provenance fields, loaded by the engine — changes go through PR review; `cost_pricing.rs` is replaced (recommended)
Keep the in-code constant table, but add `source_url` / `source_retrieved_at` / effective dates to each entry and drop substring matching
A DB table editable at runtime via a `boss cost rates set` verb
Version-controlled file as the source of truth, with a runtime DB override for urgent corrections

prompt: When SOME runs on a work item are unpriceable (unknown model, no rate epoch, capture skipped), what should the row show? The design proposes showing the priced subtotal labelled as a floor, always adjacent to the coverage ratio.
choices: Priced subtotal labelled a lower bound, with the coverage ratio always adjacent (recommended)
No figure at all unless every run on the row is priceable — refuse anything partial
Priced subtotal plus an estimated extrapolation over the unpriced runs, clearly marked as an estimate

prompt: Entry 23 in the task breakdown records backfill of the ~4017 pre-instrumentation rows as PERMANENTLY rejected (the provider transcripts are deleted) rather than deferred work. It is tagged `deferred` only because that is the tag that keeps it visible without auto-starting it. Confirm it must never be materialised into a task?

`boss cost --usd` (landed in #2596) prices every run as `input × input_rate + cache_read × cache_read_rate`, which is correct for Claude (net input) and double-charges cached input for Codex and Grok (gross input). It is safe today only because no Codex or Grok family is in the pricing table; adding one would silently mis-price every such row under an ESTIMATE label. It also prices all cache writes at one flat rate although the capture layer records the 5m/1h split. Entry 24 proposes making the estimator refuse those rows (`capture_unnormalised`, `unsplit_cache_write`) before Layer 1 lands. Confirm?
choices: Yes — refuse and name the cause, as with unknown models today; no USD figure over an unnormalised or unsplit row (recommended)
Refuse gross-input rows, but keep flat cache-write pricing as an accepted approximation and document it
Leave `--usd` as-is until the full pipeline lands; rely on the ESTIMATE label
